audits.resolution_reason: Seven invalid scalar calls accepted on the audited source. Keep API-contract defect unresolved. The reported schedule warning is not a wrong-label finding and reported 80 tests do not close this input-validation issue.
audits.text:
## a338acade0b5

**Reproduced defect — generator-call scalar contract.** Against the assigned
source SHA-256
`7ce8cf77ecf3c7c034ac0b5054e6735b54a5a4f3dfeff1e2b49b98118f95e414`,
`generate` accepts the same seven invalid scalar calls: boolean/float/string
seeds and boolean/negative/float/string sample indices. Each call returned a
lawful endpoint grid and passed `self_check`.

The source-bound reproduction is
`checks/audit/a338acade0b5/call-contract.json`, produced by the same reusable
probe. From `WORK/`:

```bash
python3 run_with_racket.py python3 ../checks/audit/call_contract_probe.py \
  a338acade0b5 --out ../checks/audit/a338acade0b5/call-contract.json
```

Its isolated task suite passed 80/80. The semantic gate's named
`column_span_only` rival had a valid vertical witness, but the stage exited 1
because the declared six-slot schedule was not separately enumerated; that is a
coverage/tooling warning, not evidence of a wrong label
(`checks/audit/a338acade0b5-combined/result.json`). I found no additional
semantic shortcut after checking horizontal, vertical, both diagonal
orientations, exact bar length, endpoint color irrelevance, and the declared
rival. The actionable target-local finding is the invalid call acceptance.
